xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4888: pan reload: a held reload ships a stale build and blocks newer reloads, so the operator approves twice

plan.title: pan reload: a held reload ships a stale build and blocks newer reloads, so the operator approves twice
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: A pan reload takes the restart lock, builds the origin/main it fetched at start, activates that build, then waits on the restart gate with no time limit while holding the lock. A newer pan reload (built from newer green main) is refused with 'restart in progress' and exit 2, and approving the held reload ships its stale build, so the operator approves twice (2026-11-03, twice). The banner never shows which build an approval ships.
narratives.Proposal: A pan reload keeps the pan dev path first, then resolves origin/main before the lock and records it (targetSha, supersedable:true) in the lock record, and builds exactly that commit. A newcomer that finds a supersedable pan reload holder compares targets by git ancestry: same or older => exit 0 (covered); strictly newer => it writes its own marker ~/.overdeck/reload-supersede/<pid>.json (refreshed every 2 s) and waits up to 20 minutes for the lock; diverged => exit 2. The holder checks markers inside the gate wait and steps aside only after the server atomically withdraws its gate request (new POST /api/restart-gate/withdraw, refused once an approval covers it). Stepping aside restores the previous build unless the dashboard already runs it, restarts nothing, writes no restart-status entry and exits 0. The banner, CLI wait lines and pan status show the 12-character build SHA. Full detail in .pan/drafts/PAN-4888.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No approval timeout on the restart gate; the wait stays unbounded (PAN-3729).
- No rebuild after approval (refresh-at-approval is not implemented).
- No HTTP route besides POST /api/restart-gate/withdraw; no change to the existing gate routes, their JSON shapes or RestartGateSnapshot.
- No 'main has moved past this build' indicator in the banner.
- pan restart, supervisor restart, supervisor watchdog and pan connect lock holders are never superseded and their behavior does not change.
- No CI-green check added to pan reload.
- No change to deploy-progress derivation (src/dashboard/server/services/deploy-progress.ts).
- The `pan status` restart-gate line does not change (the banner and the CLI wait message carry the build SHA).

autoDecisions.rationale: Supersede fixes both symptoms: the newer reload is no longer dropped, and the single waiting request is the newest build. Refresh-at-approval leaves newer reloads refused with exit 2 and rebuilds for minutes after the click while the gate request (20 s TTL) and claim (5 min lapse) expire.

autoDecisions.summary: Supersede requests are per-newcomer files ~/.overdeck/reload-supersede/<pid>.json, refreshed every poll
autoDecisions.rationale: The holder may still be building and not polling the gate; per-writer files mean two newcomers never overwrite or delete each other's request (critique finding 3).

autoDecisions.summary: Only supersedable 'pan reload' lock holders step aside
autoDecisions.rationale: pan restart waits on the gate before taking the lock, so pan reload is the only lock holder that waits for approval; supervisor/connect/restart holders and old-CLI reloads keep today's refusal, which also makes the first deploy of this change safe.

autoDecisions.summary: Targets are compared by git ancestry: same or older => exit 0, newer => supersede, diverged => exit 2
autoDecisions.rationale: Inequality is not an ordering; an older paused invocation must never replace a newer build (critique finding 2), and the Flywheel must not rebuild the same commit every tick.

autoDecisions.summary: Resolve origin/main before taking the lock and pin the build to it
autoDecisions.rationale: The SHA recorded in the lock must be the SHA that gets built, or the identical-SHA comparison is wrong.

autoDecisions.summary: A holder steps aside only after an atomic server-side withdraw (new POST /api/restart-gate/withdraw)
autoDecisions.rationale: An approval can land between two polls; the server serializes withdraw with approve, so an approved request is never discarded (critique finding 1).

autoDecisions.summary: Newcomer waits at most 20 minutes, polling every 2 s
autoDecisions.rationale: Long enough to cover a holder that is still building and only checks the marker at the gate; bounded so a stuck holder cannot hang the Flywheel forever.

autoDecisions.summary: A superseded holder exits 0, writes no restart-status entry and reports composer phase 'superseded'
autoDecisions.rationale: It is not a failure; a failed restart-status entry would light the Deploy ✗ chip for 15 minutes (deploy-progress.ts line 73).

autoDecisions.summary: Banner and CLI wait lines show the 12-character build SHA; pan status and a 'behind main' indicator are out of scope
autoDecisions.rationale: 12 characters match the existing build line; a behind-main indicator needs a server-side comparison and a snapshot contract change, and supersede already keeps the waiting build current. The pan status line was dropped to keep the plan within the 25-file surface limit; the issue only requires the banner.

autoDecisions.summary: A superseded holder keeps its build when the running dashboard already runs it
autoDecisions.rationale: If pan restart --now or the dashboard's restart button booted the holder's activated build during the wait, rolling back would rename dist/ and delete the worktree under the live server; /api/health buildCommit equals builtSha in that case, so the holder commits like the satisfied branch.

autoDecisions.summary: The pan dev branch runs before any target resolution
autoDecisions.rationale: A dev hot-restart needs no fetch; an unreachable origin must not block it (critique finding 4).

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5 (revised after critique). In src/cli/commands/reload.ts lift the pan dev branch out of the try so it runs right after the agent warning and before any target resolution: plain acquireRestartLock('pan reload'), today's refusal, today's SIGUSR2 block, release, return; no fetch. Then, when !skipBuild, resolve repoRoot and targetSha (resolveOriginMainSha), failing with '<message> — old dashboard left running', a failed status and exit 1. Call acquireReloadLock(targetSha, { isAncestor: (a, d) => isAncestorCommit(repoRoot, a, d) }): 'covered' prints the already-building-or-waiting line and returns with no status entry and exit 0 (composer phase stays 'completed'; accepted); 'refused' prints the message, records a failed status and exits 2; 'acquired' continues.
